question: How does the Gospel of Mark dramatically open its narrative concerning the Lord Jesus Christ?
opt1: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God;
opt2: The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
opt3: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
opt4: Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to set forth in order a declaration.
correct: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God;
explanation: Mark begins immediately with the good news of Jesus Christ as the Son of God: Mark 1:1 (KJV) - "The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God;"

question: Which two Old Testament prophetic voices are combined in Mark 1:2-3 to introduce the forerunner of the Messiah?
opt1: Moses and Samuel
opt2: As it is written in the prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee. The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
opt3: David and Solomon
opt4: Ezekiel and Daniel
correct: As it is written in the prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee. The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
explanation: Mark 1:2-3 quotes Malachi 3:1 and Isaiah 40:3: Mark 1:3 (KJV) - "The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight."

question: What was the austere clothing and diet of John the Baptist as he preached the baptism of repentance in the wilderness?
opt1: A coat of woven wool and shoes of badger skin; and his food was unleavened barley bread
opt2: A linen tunic with a purple girdle; and his food was figs and cluster of raisins
opt3: John was clothed with camel's hair, and with a girdle of a skin about his loins; and he did eat locusts and wild honey;
opt4: A mantle of sheepskin and sandals of wood; and his food was parched corn and oil
correct: John was clothed with camel's hair, and with a girdle of a skin about his loins; and he did eat locusts and wild honey;
explanation: Mark 1:6 describes John's prophetic attire and sustenance: Mark 1:6 (KJV) - "And John was clothed with camel's hair, and with a girdle of a skin about his loins; and he did eat locusts and wild honey;"

question: How did John contrast his water baptism with the baptism that the mightier One coming after him would administer?
opt1: John with tears of sorrow; He with the trumpet of royal victory
opt2: John with water from Jordan; He with consecrated oil from the altar
opt3: John with the law of Moses; He with signs and wonders upon Mount Zion
opt4: I indeed have baptized you with water: but he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost.
correct: I indeed have baptized you with water: but he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost.
explanation: Mark 1:8 records John's testimony concerning the Holy Spirit baptism: Mark 1:8 (KJV) - "I indeed have baptized you with water: but he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost."

question: What divine phenomena took place when Jesus came up straightway out of the water at His baptism in Jordan?
opt1: he saw the heavens opened, and the Spirit like a dove descending upon him: And there came a voice from heaven, saying, Thou art my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
opt2: A pillar of cloud rested upon the river and angels sang hymns of glory
opt3: The waters of Jordan ceased flowing and fire fell upon the bank
opt4: A great earthquake shook the wilderness and John fell upon his face
correct: he saw the heavens opened, and the Spirit like a dove descending upon him: And there came a voice from heaven, saying, Thou art my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
explanation: Mark 1:10-11 records the glorious Trinitarian manifestation at Christ's baptism: Mark 1:11 (KJV) - "And there came a voice from heaven, saying, Thou art my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."

question: What unique detail does Mark 1:13 provide regarding Jesus' forty days of temptation in the wilderness?
opt1: He slept in a deep cavern near the brook Cherith
opt2: he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto him.
opt3: He was accompanied by two disciples who fasted with Him
opt4: He wrote the words of the new covenant upon stones in the desert
correct: he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto him.
explanation: Mark alone notes that Jesus was 'with the wild beasts' in the wilderness: Mark 1:13 (KJV) - "And he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto him."

question: What inaugural message did Jesus preach in Galilee after John was put in prison in Mark 1:14-15?
opt1: The temple of Solomon shall be rebuilt in three days
opt2: Fear God and give glory to Him, for the day of vengeance is come
opt3: The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.
opt4: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord
correct: The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.
explanation: Mark 1:15 summarizes Christ's foundational gospel proclamation: Mark 1:15 (KJV) - "And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel."

question: What call did Jesus extend unto Simon and Andrew his brother as they cast a net into the sea of Galilee?
opt1: Sell all your vessels and give the silver to the poor in Capernaum
opt2: Take your nets and sail unto the coasts of Tyre and Sidon
opt3: Offer two turtledoves at the temple before following my footsteps
opt4: Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.
correct: Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.
explanation: Mark 1:17 captures the memorable apostolic invitation: Mark 1:17 (KJV) - "And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men."

question: What cry did the man with an unclean spirit utter in the synagogue of Capernaum before Jesus cast him out?
opt1: Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.
opt2: Depart from this holy place, for the law of Moses forbiddeth thee to enter
opt3: Why hast thou come with twelve disciples to disturb our assembly?
opt4: Art thou the King of Israel that shall cast out the Roman legions?
correct: Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.
explanation: Mark 1:24 records the demonic acknowledgment of Jesus as the Holy One of God: Mark 1:24 (KJV) - "Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God."

question: When a leper knelt and besought Jesus saying, 'If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean', with what compassion and words did Jesus cleanse him?
opt1: He directed him to bathe in the pool of Bethesda seven times
opt2: Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean. And as soon as he had spoken, immediately the leprosy departed from him
opt3: He sent word to the priest in Jerusalem to offer the two birds of cleansing
opt4: He spoke a word of blessing from afar and commanded him to rejoice
correct: Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean. And as soon as he had spoken, immediately the leprosy departed from him
explanation: Mark 1:41-42 highlights Christ's compassionate touch and authoritative power: Mark 1:41 (KJV) - "And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean."

question: In Capernaum, how did four men bring a man sick of the palsy unto Jesus when they could not come nigh unto Him for the press?
opt1: They carried him through the rear courtyard of the synagogue
opt2: They waited until evening when the crowds dispersed from the house
opt3: they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay.
opt4: They called upon Peter to open a passage through the multitude
correct: they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay.
explanation: Mark 2:4 records the extraordinary determination and faith of the four friends: Mark 2:4 (KJV) - "And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay."

question: What did Jesus say unto the sick of the palsy when He saw their collective faith in Mark 2:5?
opt1: Arise, take up thy staff, and return to thy family in peace
opt2: Thy faith hath exceeded the righteousness of the scribes
opt3: Go thy way into the temple and offer the sacrifice of thanksgiving
opt4: Son, thy sins be forgiven thee.
correct: Son, thy sins be forgiven thee.
explanation: Mark 2:5 reveals that Jesus addressed the man's deepest spiritual need first: Mark 2:5 (KJV) - "When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee."

question: How did Jesus prove to the questioning scribes that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins in Mark 2:9-11?
opt1: Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk? But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins... I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy bed, and go thy way into thine house.
opt2: By calling down fire upon the hearth of the house before all the people
opt3: By reciting the genealogical line of David back to Abraham
opt4: By quoting the priestly regulations concerning the Day of Atonement
correct: Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk? But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins... I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy bed, and go thy way into thine house.
explanation: Mark 2:9-11 demonstrates Christ's divine authority by validating His invisible spiritual power with visible physical healing: Mark 2:10 (KJV) - "But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (he saith to the sick of the palsy,)"

question: Whom did Jesus call to follow Him as he sat at the receipt of custom in Mark 2:14?
opt1: Zacchaeus of Jericho
opt2: Levi the son of Alphaeus
opt3: Nicodemus the ruler
opt4: Joseph of Arimathaea
correct: Levi the son of Alphaeus
explanation: Mark 2:14 identifies Levi (Matthew) as the tax collector called by Jesus: Mark 2:14 (KJV) - "And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him."

question: What celebrated aphorism did Jesus utter when the scribes and Pharisees criticized Him for eating with publicans and sinners?
opt1: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise, but a companion of fools shall be destroyed
opt2: The tree is known by his fruit, whether it be good or corrupt
opt3: They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
opt4: Cast not your holy things before swine lest they turn and rend you
correct: They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
explanation: Mark 2:17 articulates Christ's redemptive mission as the Great Physician of sinners: Mark 2:17 (KJV) - "When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance."

question: How did Jesus explain why His disciples did not fast while the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fasted?
opt1: Fasting is abolished until the destruction of the temple of Herod
opt2: My disciples are poor fishermen who must eat daily to labor at sea
opt3: The law of fasting applyeth only during the solemn month of Tishri
opt4: Can the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast. But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.
correct: Can the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast. But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.
explanation: Mark 2:19-20 associates Christ's presence with joyous wedding celebration, foretelling future fasting after His departure: Mark 2:19 (KJV) - "And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast."

question: What dual illustrations in Mark 2:21-22 teach that the new covenant gospel cannot be confined within old ritualistic forms?
opt1: No man also seweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment... And no man putteth new wine into old bottles: else the new wine doth burst the bottles
opt2: No man buildeth an altar of hewn stone, nor lighteth a censer with strange fire
opt3: No man poureth fresh milk into an unwashed vessel, nor planteth wheat among weeds
opt4: No man reapeth corn before the ear is ripe, nor mended a net with unspun flax
correct: No man also seweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment... And no man putteth new wine into old bottles: else the new wine doth burst the bottles
explanation: Mark 2:21-22 portrays the incompatibility of the vibrant New Covenant with rigid old forms: Mark 2:22 (KJV) - "And no man putteth new wine into old bottles: else the new wine doth burst the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will be marred: but new wine must be put into new bottles."

question: When the Pharisees complained that Jesus' disciples plucked corn on the Sabbath, which high priest's days did Jesus mention in citing David eating the shewbread?
opt1: In the days of Zadok the priest
opt2: in the days of Abiathar the high priest
opt3: In the days of Phinehas the son of Eleazar
opt4: In the days of Eli the judge
correct: in the days of Abiathar the high priest
explanation: Mark 2:26 specifies Abiathar in the historical reference to 1 Samuel 21: Mark 2:26 (KJV) - "How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the shewbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him?"

question: What principle regarding the divine purpose of the Sabbath does Jesus establish in Mark 2:27?
opt1: The Sabbath was instituted only for the generation that left Egypt
opt2: The Sabbath is an unbending law before which human life must yield
opt3: The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:
opt4: The Sabbath ceaseth whenever a man journeyeth into a Gentile land
correct: The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:
explanation: Mark 2:27 establishes that the Sabbath was created by God as a gracious blessing for human rest, not a burdensome yoke: Mark 2:27 (KJV) - "And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:"

question: What climactic statement of Messianic supremacy closes Mark 2:28?
opt1: Therefore the disciples are exempt from all temple taxes
opt2: Therefore the law of Moses is fulfilled in one word
opt3: Therefore let no man judge you in meat or drink
opt4: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
correct: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
explanation: Mark 2:28 declares Christ's sovereign lordship over the sacred day of rest: Mark 2:28 (KJV) - "Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath."

question: What emotion did Jesus experience toward the critics when healing the man with the withered hand on the Sabbath in Mark 3:5?
opt1: And when he had looked round about on them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their hearts, he saith unto the man, Stretch forth thine hand.
opt2: He was moved with fear and withdrew immediately to the seaside
opt3: He wept bitterly before the elders of the synagogue
opt4: He marveled at their profound knowledge of the oral traditions
correct: And when he had looked round about on them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their hearts, he saith unto the man, Stretch forth thine hand.
explanation: Mark 3:5 uniquely records Christ's holy anger combined with grief over their hardhearted legalism: Mark 3:5 (KJV) - "And when he had looked round about on them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their hearts, he saith unto the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it out: and his hand was restored whole as the other."

question: With which political group did the Pharisees immediately take counsel against Jesus to destroy Him in Mark 3:6?
opt1: The Roman centurions of Caesarea
opt2: the Herodians
opt3: The Essenes of the wilderness
opt4: The Samaritan council of Sychar
correct: the Herodians
explanation: Mark 3:6 records the unlikely alliance between religious Pharisees and political Herodians to destroy Jesus: Mark 3:6 (KJV) - "And the Pharisees went forth, and straightway took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him."

question: What confession did unclean spirits make when they fell down before Jesus in Mark 3:11?
opt1: Thou art the prophet that should come into the wilderness
opt2: Thou art the Son of David who shall reign in Jerusalem
opt3: Thou art the Son of God.
opt4: Thou art the judge of the living and the dead
correct: Thou art the Son of God.
explanation: Mark 3:11 shows demons compelled to confess Christ's supreme divine identity: Mark 3:11 (KJV) - "And unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, saying, Thou art the Son of God."

question: For what dual primary purposes did Jesus ordain the twelve apostles in Mark 3:14-15?
opt1: To collect the tithes of Galilee and build new houses of prayer
opt2: To debate the doctors of the law and translate the holy scriptures
opt3: To govern the provinces of Judaea and appoint local magistrates
opt4: that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach, And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils:
correct: that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach, And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils:
explanation: Mark 3:14-15 defines apostolic ministry as intimate companionship with Christ followed by preaching and spiritual deliverance: Mark 3:14 (KJV) - "And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,"

question: What surname did Jesus bestow upon James and John the sons of Zebedee in Mark 3:17?
opt1: Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:
opt2: Barnabas, which is, The sons of consolation
opt3: Bar-jona, which is, The sons of the dove
opt4: Didymus, which is, The sons of the twin
correct: Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:
explanation: Mark 3:17 gives the Aramaic surname Boanerges meaning sons of thunder: Mark 3:17 (KJV) - "And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:"

question: What did Jesus' friends or family say when they went out to lay hold on Him because the multitude prevented them from eating bread?
opt1: He hath made Himself equal with the kings of the Gentiles
opt2: He is beside himself.
opt3: He hath forgotten the covenant of His fathers
opt4: He is planning to lead an insurrection against Rome
correct: He is beside himself.
explanation: Mark 3:21 uniquely records His family's misunderstanding, thinking He was out of His mind: Mark 3:21 (KJV) - "And when his friends heard of it, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself."

question: What malicious accusation did the scribes who came down from Jerusalem make against Jesus in Mark 3:22?
opt1: He deceiveth the people through Greek sorceries
opt2: He hath broken the sabbath thirty and nine times
opt3: He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casteth he out devils.
opt4: He hath stolen the sacred scrolls from the temple library
correct: He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casteth he out devils.
explanation: Mark 3:22 records the blasphemous charge linking Christ's miracles to Beelzebub: Mark 3:22 (KJV) - "And the scribes which came down from Jerusalem said, He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casteth he out devils."

question: With what logical kingdom principle did Jesus dismantle their absurd accusation in Mark 3:24-25?
opt1: The strong man must first give his silver to the poor before his goods are spoiled

correct: And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand. And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
explanation: Mark 3:24-25 shows the internal collapse of any realm divided against itself: Mark 3:24 (KJV) - "And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand."

question: Why did Jesus issue the terrifying warning concerning eternal damnation for blasphemy against the Holy Ghost in Mark 3:29-30?
opt1: Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.
opt2: Because they refused to pay the temple tax at Capernaum
opt3: Because they doubted the resurrection of the dead
opt4: Because they prevented the children from entering the synagogue
correct: Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.
explanation: Mark 3:30 gives the exact reason: attributing the Holy Spirit's miraculous work to an unclean demon: Mark 3:30 (KJV) - "Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit."

question: How did Jesus redefine His true spiritual family when told that His mother and brethren stood without seeking Him?
opt1: He declared that all citizens of Nazareth were His brethren
opt2: whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.
opt3: He said that the twelve apostles alone were His physical household
opt4: He stated that genealogy no longer mattered after the exile in Babylon
correct: whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.
explanation: Mark 3:35 places spiritual obedience to God's will above biological kinship: Mark 3:35 (KJV) - "For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother."

question: From where did Jesus teach the great multitude by the seaside in Mark 4:1?
opt1: From the roof of a fisherman's cottage near the harbor

opt4: From the steps of the local synagogue facing the shore

explanation: Mark 4:1 describes Jesus using a boat as an offshore pulpit: Mark 4:1 (KJV) - "And he began again to teach by the sea side: and there was gathered unto him a great multitude, so that he entered into a ship, and sat in the sea; and the whole multitude was by the sea on the land."

question: In the Parable of the Sower (Mark 4:3-8), what different yields did the good ground bring forth?
opt1: Tenfold, twentyfold, and thirtyfold

opt3: A hundredfold, two hundredfold, and five hundredfold
opt4: some thirty, and some sixty, and some an hundred.

question: What sovereign distinction did Jesus make between His disciples and those outside regarding the kingdom of God in Mark 4:11?
opt1: Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables:

opt3: The disciples are justified by circumcision while outsiders must keep seventy fasts
opt4: The mysteries of heaven are reserved only for the sons of Levi and Aaron

question: In explaining the Sower, what three destructive influences does Jesus identify as choking the word among the thorns in Mark 4:19?
opt1: False prophets, idolatrous altars, and foreign taxation

question: What rhetorical question does Jesus ask in Mark 4:21 regarding the proper purpose and placement of a candle?

explanation: Mark 4:21 illustrates the open, illuminating purpose of divine truth: Mark 4:21 (KJV) - "And he said unto them, Is a candle brought to be put under a bushel, or under a bed? and not to be set on a candlestick?"

question: What principle of spiritual reciprocation does Jesus give in Mark 4:24-25 concerning hearing and receiving truth?
opt1: He that speaketh much shall have his words recorded in the temple

opt3: Knowledge increaseth only by studying the traditions of the elders
opt4: with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given. For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he hath.

question: What unique parable found only in Mark 4:26-29 portrays the mysterious, spontaneous growth of God's kingdom?
opt1: So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground; And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how. For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.

opt4: The parable of the two sons who were sent to prune the branches of the olive tree

explanation: The Parable of the Seed Growing Secretly is found exclusively in Mark: Mark 4:28 (KJV) - "For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear."

question: To what does Jesus liken the kingdom of God in Mark 4:31-32, emphasizing its immense growth from the smallest origin?
opt1: To a grain of wheat falling into the earth and dying

opt4: To an olive branch grafted into the stem of Jesse

explanation: Mark 4:31-32 illustrates the global expansion of the kingdom from tiny beginnings: Mark 4:32 (KJV) - "But when it is sown, it groweth up, and becometh greater than all herbs, and shooteth out great branches; so that the fowls of the air may lodge under the shadow of it."
